summary: Build practical skills for gender-transformative male engagement, GBV prevention, safeguarding, and measurement. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Engaging men and boys in gender equality programming means designing interventions that address social norms, power and accountability. Designed for gender advisers, GBV prevention specialists, safeguarding managers and youth programme leads, the course develops skills to assess gender norms, build a theory of change, plan safe facilitation and referral pathways, and monitor outcomes with gender-sensitive indicators.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who plan, fund, deliver, safeguard, evaluate, or communicate gender equality programming involving men and boys. It suits experienced practitioners who need stronger analytical and implementation discipline rather than an introductory overview.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working experience in gender equality, GBV prevention, safeguarding, youth programming, community engagement, monitoring and evaluation, or related programme management. You should be able to read a theory of change and interpret basic programme indicators. No coding or programming is required. Advanced concepts such as digital monitoring, AI-assisted qualitative coding, and norm measurement are taught at operational application level, not technical engineering level.
